title: API conformance harness for streaming, function-calls, and structured outputs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: As we broaden supported API features (streaming, tool/function calls, structured outputs, and compatibility layers for older SDKs), intermittent regressions have surfaced when models or runtime kernels change. We need a durable, extensible conformance and regression test harness that: 1) codifies golden prompts and expected structured outputs across model variants, 2) validates streaming semantics (chunk ordering, partial tokens, finalization tokens), 3) verifies tool/function calling contracts (signature, required/optional params, error responses), and 4) runs as part of CI against both hosted and dedicated runtime variants. Scope: - Build golden-prompt suites representing edge cases for streaming (long prefixes, mid-stream tool calls, interleaved JSON fragments) - Implement contract tests that assert compatible wire-level behavior for SDKs v1.x and v2.x compatibility layer - Add structured-output schema validation (JSON Schema) for function outputs and nested tool-calls - CI jobs to run fast smoke and nightly exhaustive matrices across models/quantizations/out-of-order chunking simulations Out of scope: load/throughput performance tuning (handled by ENG infra perf track) and private deployment infra provisioning. Success metrics: - CI prevents at least 95% of regressions that previously reached staging (measured by number of reverted deploys) - Golden-suite coverage in PR checks (fast subset) within 10 minutes and nightly full run completion under 3 hours
acceptance_criteria: A golden-prompt JSON corpus exists with at least 120 prompts covering streaming, function calls, nested structured outputs, and edge cases
Contract tests assert wire-level compatibility for streaming chunk framing, content-type negotiation, and function-call JSON shapes for SDK v1.x and v2.x
CI exposes two gates: PR-fast (subset of golden prompts) and nightly-full (complete matrix). Both must pass for release promotion
Failures include deterministic diffs and links to reproduction harness logs with deterministic replay
Test harness supports simulated partial chunk delivery and network jitter to reproduce real-world streaming failures
test_plan: Create golden prompts with expected normalized outputs (strip timestamps, session-ids) and store under /tests/golden/api-conformance/
Implement contract test runner (Go) that: validates streaming frames, validates function-call signature and param types, and applies JSON Schema validation on structured outputs
Add SDK compatibility checks: run tests against upstream v1 shim and v2 native SDK in CI matrix
Build a small in-process stream fuzzer to inject mid-stream truncation, duplicate frames, and reordered frames to confirm harness detects out-of-order/incomplete behavior
Wire test runner into GitHub Actions: PR-fast uses a 15-prompt subset across 3 model variants; nightly runs full corpus across quantized and FP16 model variants
Record golden outputs across model versions and provide a curated 'approved changes' workflow that requires explicit owner approval for any golden updates
implementation_notes: Decision: Use JSON Schema for structured outputs rather than custom parsers to keep validation short and declarative
Trade-off: PR-fast subset must be small enough to keep feedback under 10 minutes; selected prompts prioritize tool-calls and streaming flush semantics
Mocking: We'll implement a streaming transport shim that can run in-process for CI and a separate integration mode that targets staged runtime endpoints (hosted/dedicated)
Data storage: Golden corpus stored in repo under /tests/golden with metadata files that include allowed fuzz tolerances (tokenization differences, whitespace)
Observability: On failures, tests upload trimmed logs and a replay script to S3 and open a browser-friendly link in the CI job output
PR references: initial implementation PR will be linked here when available (WIP)
